import argparse
import sys
from .storage import (
    add_note,
    delete_note,
    find_notes,
    list_notes,
    tag_note,
)
from .models import Note


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Command-line note taking application")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", help="Available commands")

    # Add command
    parser_add = subparsers.add_parser("add", help="Add a new note")
    parser_add.add_argument("title", help="Title of the note")
    parser_add.add_argument("content", help="Content of the note")
    parser_add.add_argument("-t", "--tags", nargs="*", help="Tags for the note", default=[])

    # List command
    parser_list = subparsers.add_parser("list", help="List all notes")

    # Search command
    parser_search = subparsers.add_parser("search", help="Search notes by keyword")
    parser_search.add_argument("keyword", help="Keyword to search in title and content")

    # Delete command
    parser_delete = subparsers.add_parser("delete", help="Delete a note by ID")
    parser_delete.add_argument("id", type=int, help="ID of the note to delete")

    # Tag command
    parser_tag = subparsers.add_parser("tag", help="Add a tag to a note")
    parser_tag.add_argument("id", type=int, help="ID of the note to tag")
    parser_tag.add_argument("tag", help="Tag to add")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.command == "add":
        # Generate a new ID: if there are existing notes, max ID + 1, else 1
        notes = list_notes()
        new_id = max([note.id for note in notes]) + 1 if notes else 1
        note = Note(id=new_id, title=args.title, content=args.content, tags=args.tags)
        add_note(note)
        print(f"Note added with ID {new_id}")

    elif args.command == "list":
        notes = list_notes()
        if not notes:
            print("No notes found.")
            return
        for note in notes:
            tags_str = f" [Tags: {', '.join(note.tags)}]" if note.tags else ""
            print(f"{note.id}: {note.title}{tags_str}")

    elif args.command == "search":
        notes = find_notes(args.keyword)
        if not notes:
            print(f"No notes found for keyword '{args.keyword}'.")
            return
        for note in notes:
            tags_str = f" [Tags: {', '.join(note.tags)}]" if note.tags else ""
            print(f"{note.id}: {note.title}{tags_str}")

    elif args.command == "delete":
        if delete_note(args.id):
            print(f"Note with ID {args.id} deleted.")
        else:
            print(f"No note found with ID {args.id}.")

    elif args.command == "tag":
        if tag_note(args.id, args.tag):
            print(f"Tag '{args.tag}' added to note {args.id}.")
        else:
            print(f"No note found with ID {args.id}.")

    else:
        parser.print_help()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import os
import tempfile
import pytest
from notekeeper.storage import (
    load_notes,
    save_notes,
    add_note,
    delete_note,
    find_notes,
    list_notes,
    tag_note,
)
from notekeeper.models import Note


@pytest.fixture
def isolated_storage(monkeypatch, tmpdir):
    """Isolate the storage file for each test."""
    # Create a temporary file for notes
    temp_file = tmpdir.join("notes.json")
    # Monkeypatch the DATA_FILE in the storage module
    monkeypatch.setattr("notekeeper.storage.DATA_FILE", str(temp_file))
    # Ensure the file starts empty
    with open(temp_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump([], f)
    yield temp_file
    # Teardown: remove the file if needed (tmpdir is cleaned automatically)


def test_add_note(isolated_storage):
    note = Note(id=1, title="Test", content="Test content")
    add_note(note)
    notes = load_notes()
    assert len(notes) == 1
    assert notes[0].title == "Test"


def test_list_notes(isolated_storage):
    # Start with empty
    assert list_notes() == []
    # Add two notes
    note1 = Note(id=1, title="First", content="First note")
    note2 = Note(id=2, title="Second", content="Second note")
    add_note(note1)
    add_note(note2)
    notes = list_notes()
    assert len(notes) == 2
    assert notes[0].title == "First"
    assert notes[1].title == "Second"


def test_find_notes(isolated_storage):
    note1 = Note(id=1, title="Hello world", content="Some content")
    note2 = Note(id=2, title="Another note", content="Hello again")
    add_note(note1)
    add_note(note2)
    # Search for "hello"
    results = find_notes("hello")
    assert len(results) == 2
    # Search for "world"
    results = find_notes("world")
    assert len(results) == 1
    assert results[0].id == 1
    # Search for non-existent
    results = find_notes("xyz")
    assert len(results) == 0


def test_delete_note(isolated_storage):
    note = Note(id=1, title="To delete", content="Will be deleted")
    add_note(note)
    # Delete it
    assert delete_note(1) is True
    assert len(load_notes()) == 0
    # Try to delete again
    assert delete_note(1) is False


def test_tag_note(isolated_storage):
    note = Note(id=1, title="Tag me", content="Content", tags=[])
    add_note(note)
    # Add a tag
    assert tag_note(1, "important") is True
    notes = load_notes()
    assert notes[0].tags == ["important"]
    # Add same tag again (should not duplicate)
    tag_note(1, "important")
    notes = load_notes()
    assert notes[0].tags == ["important"]
    # Add another tag
    tag_note(1, "review")
    notes = load_notes()
    assert set(notes[0].tags) == {"important", "review"}
    # Try to tag non-existent note
    assert tag_note(999, "test") is False

# NoteKeeper

A simple command-line note taking application.

## Features

- Add notes with title, content, and optional tags
- List all notes
- Search notes by keyword
- Delete notes by ID
- Add tags to existing notes

## Installation

```bash
pip install .
```

## Usage

### Add a note

```bash
notekeeper add "My Title" "My note content" -t tag1 tag2
```

### List notes

```bash
notekeeper list
```

### Search notes

```bash
notekeeper search keyword
```

### Delete a note

```bash
notekeeper delete 1
```

### Tag a note

```bash
notekeeper tag 1 important
```

## Running Tests

```bash
pytest
```

import sys
import pytest
from notekeeper.cli import main
from notekeeper.storage import load_notes
from notekeeper.models import Note


def test_cli_add(monkeypatch, tmpdir, capsys):
    # Isolate storage
    temp_file = tmpdir.join("notes.json")
    monkeypatch.setattr("notekeeper.storage.DATA_FILE", str(temp_file))
    with open(temp_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump([], f)

    # Run add command
    test_args = ["notekeeper", "add", "Test Title", "Test Content", "-t", "tag1", "tag2"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", test_args)
    main()
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "Note added with ID 1" in captured.out

    # Check storage
    notes = load_notes()
    assert len(notes) == 1
    assert notes[0].title == "Test Title"
    assert notes[0].content == "Test Content"
    assert set(notes[0].tags) == {"tag1", "tag2"}


def test_cli_list(monkeypatch, tmpdir, capsys):
    temp_file = tmpdir.join("notes.json")
    monkeypatch.setattr("notekeeper.storage.DATA_FILE", str(temp_file))
    with open(temp_file, "w") as f:

    note = Note(id=1, title="List Test", content="Content")

    # Run list command
    test_args = ["notekeeper", "list"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", test_args)
    main()
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "1: List Test" in captured.out


def test_cli_search(monkeypatch, tmpdir, capsys):
    temp_file = tmpdir.join("notes.json")
    monkeypatch.setattr("notekeeper.storage.DATA_FILE", str(temp_file))
    with open(temp_file, "w") as f:

    note1 = Note(id=1, title="Hello", content="World")
    note2 = Note(id=2, title="Another", content="hello world")
    add_note(note1)
    add_note(note2)

    test_args = ["notekeeper", "search", "hello"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", test_args)
    main()
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "1: Hello" in captured.out
    assert "2: Another" in captured.out


def test_cli_delete(monkeypatch, tmpdir, capsys):
    temp_file = tmpdir.join("notes.json")
